scenarios.title: Cheapest items are not the cheapest delivered basket
scenarios.expect: Pelican has the lowest per-unit price on both items, but its $45 flat fee makes it more expensive delivered than Meadowlark.

scenarios.title: Bundling everything with one supplier saves money
scenarios.expect: Meadowlark's butter is $5.10 cheaper per case, but buying it from Bramblewood with everything else crosses Bramblewood's $500 free-delivery threshold and avoids a second delivery fee.

scenarios.title: Two suppliers required because of stock
scenarios.expect: 288 lb = 8 cases. Meadowlark and Bramblewood each have only 4 cases in stock, so the line must be split across both.

scenarios.title: Order minimum rules out an apparently cheap supplier
scenarios.expect: Kestrel is cheaper per item, but this order is far below its $400 minimum, so Citrus Row is recommended.

scenarios.title: Delivery day changes the recommendation
scenarios.expect: On Saturday only Pelican delivers. On Wednesday Kestrel also delivers, the order clears its minimum, and Kestrel is cheaper.

scenarios.title: Equivalent pack sizes are normalized
scenarios.expect: 360 eggs = 30 dozen. Meadowlark's 15-dozen case, Kestrel's 30-dozen case and Pelican's 5-dozen flat are compared on the same per-egg basis, including any overbuy.

scenarios.title: No feasible solution
scenarios.expect: Sunday 2026-11-08: no supplier delivers on Sundays. The explanation lists each supplier's delivery days.

scenarios.title: Stale price and stock are flagged
scenarios.expect: Pelican's espresso price is older than 14 days and Citrus Row's blueberry stock is older than 36 hours: both offers are excluded and flagged, never silently used.
